Two new nodes, `s7 usend` and `s7 urcv`, exchange data with the PLC instructions USEND / URCV
over an S7 connection. Upgrade if your PLC program uses USEND / URCV; existing flows work as
before.

## Highlights

- **USEND / URCV.** On an endpoint with the protocol "S7 partner" (the same S7 connection as for
  BSEND / BRCV), `s7 urcv` gives a message for each USEND of the PLC program: `msg.payload` is a
  Buffer for one area, or an array of Buffers for two to four areas. `s7 usend` sends one to four
  areas to a URCV in the PLC. USEND has no acknowledgement and must fit in one PDU; use
  `s7 bsend` for larger data. An S7-1500 URCV takes the data only when each area has the exact
  length of its receive area (for example 100 bytes for an `Array[0..99] of Byte`), so check
  `NDR` or a counter in the PLC. `s7 usend` writes to the PLC.
- **Endpoint status.** The status of an S7 partner endpoint shows how many USENDs came and how
  many `s7 brcv` / `s7 urcv` nodes listen.

Tested on PLCSIM Advanced V8 (S7-1500, FW S4.1): a PLC USEND with two areas reaches `s7 urcv`,
and 100 bytes from `s7 usend` reach the PLC URCV. See the example flow "07 - USEND and URCV".

## Upgrade notes

- None for flows. Rust crate `s7` only: `Partner::recv` now returns `Message` (a BSEND block or
  a USEND) instead of `Block`.
